items.title: Victor Rendon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: INTERVIEWEE: There was a lot of, I’m sure you have that book, “The Latin Tinge” who was the author of that? I don’t remember but you know what I’m talking about.

ctx.x: And you heard it for the next five years almost every day. So I think those days are gone, because now we’ve got too much information and you can not even listen to all that information. You don’t have enough time.

This is sort of a historical question, I don’t know if you’ll have an opinion on it. Jelly Roll Morton, you know the early jazz pianist, was quoted when people would say well what is jazz, and he would say it’s this and that, but it has to have a Spanish tinge to it. And I always wondered what he meant by that. I wonder if you have an opinion on it. To me when he says “Spanish” I think he means the music comes from south of our border. © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-
